cutoff: first public version on or before 2026-10-31

inclusion.I1: Translates C source code into Rust (C may be one of several source languages).
inclusion.I2: An LLM generates or repairs the Rust (alone or with program analysis or a rule-based translator).
inclusion.I3: The paper presents a translation pipeline that produces complete Rust for C functions, files or programs (not a benchmark, user study, empirical study of other tools, survey, single-construct tool, or optimizer of already-translated Rust).
inclusion.I4: The paper reports, for translations it produced, a success rate from an automated correctness or equivalence check (tests, differential testing or fuzzing, symbolic execution, verification). Compile rate, unsafe ratio, similarity or LLM-judge metrics alone do not count.
inclusion.I5: First public version (arXiv v1, or venue publication if not on arXiv) on or before 2026-10-31.

rules.loop: Every pipeline step in which running the program on inputs (tests, fuzzing, differential or equivalence tests, symbolic execution, verification) decides whether a candidate is repaired, regenerated, selected or accepted. Compiler-only feedback is not an input-driven loop.

precedence: n/l if there is no input-driven loop
Yes if at least one reported correctness result uses inputs the paper states were unavailable to the loop (quotable)
n/a if the evaluation check is symbolic or exhaustive only
held_out.n/l: No input-driven repair loop; evaluation inputs are held out by construction.
held_out.n/a: Symbolic check: no sampled input set to hold out.

rules.mut: Yes only if the paper injects known-wrong translations (mutants, seeded bugs, deliberately wrong translations) into its acceptance or evaluation check and reports whether the check rejects them. Recall checks against an independent oracle, coverage, and manual review are noted but coded No.
rules.regrade: R: the public artifact ships (a) the original C, (b) the Rust the system itself produced (not gold/reference Rust, not output that requires re-running an LLM), and (c) both in a form that builds and runs so that the original C can act as a differential oracle. Meets / Partial / No, by inspecting repository trees; nothing was built for systems not re-graded here. Refined in the paper: (c) means both build and run as user-space programs or libraries, the form our harness executes.
